why: Collapsing episodic and semantic memory loses the one question a learning system most needs answered: *how* did this come to be known, and what happened when it was used. A single store cannot answer it, because the field rewrites itself as weights change while the trajectory must remain intact. So memory is addressed in two dimensions — M = (R, F) — with different mutation laws and links in both directions.

R.is: Replay — temporal history, execution trajectories, prior folds, learning deltas, observed outcomes
R.mutation: R_{t+1} = R_t || e_t: append-only and versioned; an event is never rewritten

F.is: Field — semantic relationships, vector neighbourhoods, behavioural biases, graph topology, contextual relevance
F.mutation: F_{t+1} = Apply(F_t, Delta_F_t): evolves through verified deltas only

axes.why_different_laws: the field may legitimately change as understanding improves, while the trajectory that produced it must stay intact; rewriting replay would destroy the evidence the field's changes rest on

record.law: the two references let the same event be reconstructed historically or retrieved semantically

retrieval.replay_to_field: retrieve an earlier execution and reconstruct the semantic field that was active when it happened
retrieval.field_to_replay: find a relevant semantic neighbourhood and recover the trajectories that produced or modified it
retrieval.use: an agent can find a successful strategy through Field similarity and then inspect the Replay history to see which queries actually worked
retrieval.scope: both directions are scope-checked: a vector may not be read across principals, and neither may the trajectory behind it

invariants.TM1: memory is addressed in two dimensions, R and F, which are never collapsed into one another
invariants.TM2: Replay is append-only and versioned: appending advances the version, and any attempt to rewrite an existing event is refused
invariants.TM3: Field evolves only through verified deltas; an unverified delta is refused and the field version does not advance
invariants.TM4: each replay event records the field version that was active when it happened, so the semantic state at that moment can be reconstructed later
invariants.TM5: a later field change never alters what an earlier replay→field retrieval returns: history is preserved even as weights move
invariants.TM6: field→replay returns the events that produced or modified a field version, so every semantic state names its own history
invariants.TM7: both retrieval directions are scope-checked against the principal, and a cross-principal read fails in either direction
invariants.TM8: append and delta application are deterministic and return the new version, so the same sequence reproduces the same store
invariants.TM9: a verified outcome is recorded as a field event as well as a replay event, so 'what do I know' and 'how did I learn it' stay linked
invariants.TM10: the store answers both questions the design exists for: what is known, and how it was learned and what happened when it was used
